workload_shapes_reproduced: SQLite-backed agent filesystem SDK operations for files/directories, key-value state, and tool-call audit trails across Rust, Python, and TypeScript SDKs
CLI init and database-backed agent filesystem creation
agentfs run copy-on-write FUSE overlay syscall workload
interactive bash session whose writes remain out of the host filesystem
git init/add/commit/log inside the overlay with no host repository materialization
overlay readdir/unlink behavior for delta files under base directories such as .git
FUSE cache invalidation for unlink, rmdir, rename, cached-negative file create, and cached-negative directory create
symlink handling for host-visible and sandbox-created symlinks

boundaries: The first unmodified integration run under the repository process umask 0077 failed the Linux baseline syscall permission assertions; rerunning the same upstream integration suite with CI-like umask 022 passed.
Earlier AgentFS pjdfstest and xfstests records remain separate negative full-filesystem conformance evidence; this record is the positive official SDK/CLI/workspace workload evidence.
This reproduction does not claim AgentFS requires namei_ext or eBPF policy logic.
verdict: AgentFS provides a strong source-backed agent workspace workload seed: SDK state, filesystem operations, tool-call audit, FUSE mount, copy-on-write sandbox run, overlay whiteout, cache invalidation, git/bash execution, symlink behavior, and AI-framework example integration all reproduce on this host once the CI-like umask is used for permission-sensitive syscall assertions.
